habit_scope: What goes in before the slab pour: underslab plumbing, compacted granular, 6-mil poly with 12-in laps, wood out of the pour. ORNL FLOOR SLAB / radon layering; CMHC Ch7 basement floor slab sequence (Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC); HUD §4.6. A basement house still has a basement slab; a Fontana house has the first-floor slab. Radon standpipe and termite soil treatment are documented alts where the hazard exists — not a Fontana-vs-Utah fight until the book names those markets (Gap gap-P06-fontana-utah-split).
how_it_is_done: Plumbing first. CMHC Ch7: 'Complete the installation of sewer lines and other subsurface work before the slab is placed. Compact backfill in trenches.' Ch2 Stages: 'Placement of the granular layer and basement floor slab usually occurs later when the basement plumbing rough-in is completed.' Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. This is the MEP hold. Do not invent pipe sizes or a DWV schedule — CLASS is underslab plumbing.

Gravel / granular under the slab. ORNL: 'Lay minimum 4-inch-thick layer of coarse, clean gravel under slab'; radon: at least 4 in thick, clean aggregate no less than 1/2 inch in diameter. CMHC radon method: 100 mm (4 in.) layer of clean granular material under the floor-on-ground. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. HUD §4.6 (as already filed on m-P05-slab): 2–3 in sand/gravel + 6-mil — confirm AHJ; do not pick a winner between 2–3 in and 4 in.
Compact fill under the slab (ORNL FLOOR SLAB). CMHC SOG: compacted granular, no soft pockets. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.

6-mil poly on the gravel. ORNL: 6-mil (minimum) polyethylene beneath the slab on top of the gravel drainage bed; edges lapped at least 12 inches; extend over the top of the footing or sealed to the foundation wall; slit an 'x' for penetrations, turn up the tabs and tape them; avoid punctures — rounded riverbed gravel if possible. Optional 2-in sand layer on top of the poly (improves curing, some puncture protection) — optional, not a second Method. CMHC: 0.15 mm (6 mil) polyethylene under the floor. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
Wood out of the pour. ORNL DECAY AND TERMITE: 'Remove all grade stakes, spreader sticks, and wood embedded in concrete during pour.' Form wood out of the pour (ORNL).

Caulk slab/wall and pipe penetrations. ORNL: tool the joint between wall and slab and seal with polyurethane caulk; 1/2-in gap around plumbing/utility lead-ins through the slab, filled with polyurethane or similar. CMHC: seal the floor-to-wall joint to keep radon from entering. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
Isolation joint at the wall; slab floats — do not sit it on a wall ledge (ORNL note 16 / P05 D6). Isolation joints at wall perimeter and column pads (ORNL FLOOR SLAB).

Radon standpipe and termite soil treatment are the documented alts (m-P06-radon-standpipe, m-P06-termite-soil-treat). Do not invent a Fontana-vs-Utah split — ORNL only says 'in some regions termite control may be considered more critical than thermal considerations, while the reverse is true elsewhere.' Gap gap-P06-fontana-utah-split.
trades: CMHC: plumbing rough-in before the granular/slab. ORNL: construction contractor. No crew size. Electrical/mechanical by qualified personnel (CMHC Ch1) — not a headcount.
tools_equipment: Not a SKU list. Named: poly, gravel, caulk, form wood that must come out.
inspection_hold_points: Sewer/subsurface work in; trench backfill compacted (CMHC) before the slab.
Gravel in; 6-mil poly lapped 12 in; sealed to wall or over footing (ORNL).
Grade stakes, spreader sticks, and form wood out of the pour (ORNL).
Soil treatment before slab if that alt is in play (ORNL: do not disturb treated soil prior to pouring). Form wood out.
Radon standpipe in the gravel, capped, if that alt is in play (ORNL).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit under any slab — basement floor or SOG. Radon pipe and termite treatment are the documented add/alts where the hazard exists.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Pouring before plumbing is in. Leaving wood in the slab. Skipping poly. Inventing a Fontana-vs-Utah split the books did not name.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — gravel and visqueen. What they skip is 12-in laps sealed to the wall, wood out, and plumbing in first.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Radon path and termite treatment belong on the drawings. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Not a stamp.
risk_if_swapped_late: Adding radon or termite after the slab is a retrofit. ORNL: completing the vent stack during construction is normally less costly than after finish. Catch on the drawings.
plain_language_summary: Before the slab: plumbing in, trenches compacted, gravel down, 6-mil poly lapped 12 inches and stuck to the wall, wood out of the pour. A Utah basement still gets a basement slab; a Fontana house gets the first-floor slab. Same prep. Radon pipe and termite spray are extras the books name where the hazard exists — not a market fight we invented.
spanish_summary: Antes de la losa: plomería adentro, zanjas compactadas, grava, polietileno de 6 mil con traslape de 12 pulgadas sellado a la pared, sin madera en el vaciado. El sótano de Utah también lleva losa; Fontana lleva la losa de primer piso. Tubo de radón y termita son extras donde el libro nombra el riesgo.
locators: ORNL BFH §2.2 radon film 6-mil, 12-in laps; FLOOR SLAB checklist compact fill / vapor retarder; DECAY AND TERMITE remove grade stakes
CMHC Ch7 usual construction sequence for a concrete floor slab: sewer first, compact trenches, 0.15 mm (6 mil) poly (printed pp 80–82)
CMHC Ch2: granular layer and basement slab after basement plumbing rough-in
confidence_notes: Sequence agreed across ORNL and CMHC. 4 in vs 2–3 in gravel both printed — confirm AHJ. Market split Gap. On SOG this work is before the P05 pour in the field; spine P05→P06 not rewritten.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring, demo of an existing house) are not a sequence in CMHC/ORNL/HUD/FM — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods. Essential Guide is framing-only (opened 2026-08-30; silent on site/layout). B&D Room Additions not used as a P00–P06 sequence.

certs: qualified personnel for electrical/mechanical (CMHC Ch1) — not a license number

labor_notes: CMHC names qualified personnel for electrical/mechanical. Licensed termiticide applicator not named (same as P05). Crew Gap.
layering: Plumbing/sewer in compacted trenches → min 4-in clean gravel (ORNL) → 6-mil poly, 12-in laps, sealed to wall → optional 2-in sand → slab. Wood out.
Basement slab isolation joint at wall; slab floats (ORNL / P05 D6).
CMHC 6 mil / 4 in granular is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
code_to_check: CMHC 2010 NBC radon methods — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not copy 200 Bq/m3 as an EPA number.
HUD §4.6 / ACI 302 as already filed on P05 slab. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Do not invent R506.
time_money: ORNL: running the radon stack during construction is normally less costly than after finish. No dollars. No invented days.

walkthroughs.title: Perkins Builder Brothers Ep.4 (underslab prep)
walkthroughs.what_it_shows: Field 1000 sf 2-story: tamp gravel then 6 mil then steel. Same house as other Perkins clips.

images.caption: CMHC Fig 49: well-compacted fill under slab; dampproofing; floor-to-wall joint and caulking; poly/air-vapour path. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Layering: compacted fill then slab; joint sealed. 6 in above grade is CMHC; ORNL ≥8 in is the US handbook — confirm AHJ.

inspector_looks_for: Min 4-in clean gravel (ORNL) or 4-in granular (CMHC — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC). HUD 2–3 in sand/gravel is the other printed number — confirm AHJ; do not pick a winner.
No wood left in the pour (ORNL).
inspector_fails: Wood left in the pour — ORNL: remove all grade stakes, spreader sticks, and wood embedded in concrete during pour.
Disturbing treated soil before the pour when termiticide was used (ORNL: 'Do not disturb treated soil prior to pouring concrete slab').
common_messups: Puncturing the poly on sharp gravel (ORNL: consider rounded riverbed gravel).
Leaving form wood / grade stakes in the slab (ORNL).
Connecting roof leaders to the foundation drain (already P05; ORNL separate surface/roof/foundation drains).
do_not_cheap: 6-mil poly, 12-in laps, sealed to the wall (hold + layering).
Plumbing in and trenches compacted before the pour (hold).
Gravel under the slab (layering). Confirm 4 in vs HUD 2–3 in with AHJ — do not pick a winner.
Permit gate: radon and termite path on the drawings (P00/P02).
smart_save: Optional 2-in sand over the poly is ORNL optional, not a required extra Method. No dollars.
HUD 2–3 in vs ORNL 4 in gravel — confirm AHJ; not a field cheap-out.
Late swap: adding a radon stack after the slab is the retrofit ORNL says costs more than running the stack during construction.
sop_gap_note: Fastener_schedule [] — caulk and poly, not nails. walkthroughs []. Fontana vs Utah radon/termite split is Gap. On SOG, this Method is before the pour in the field even though the spine reads P05→P06.
